actions.description: The declared re-enable after a safety reset: switch joint_trajectory_controller on again through /controller_manager/switch_controller (STRICT), so the trajectory the e-stop dropped is not resumed. On activation the controller holds the state it starts from: the last command-interface values when set_last_command_interface_value_as_state_on_activation (true by default) applies and every state interface has a command interface, else the measured joints. With this deployment's position-only command interface (position and velocity states) that is the measured position; a configuration that also commanded velocity would hold the last position command, which can differ from the measured position

facts.text: The repository contains a Gazebo Fortress simulation for a 7-DOF robotic arm with ROS 2 Control integration and MoveIt motion planning.
The README calls bcr_arm.gazebo.launch.py the primary launch file and says it uses ROS 2 mock controllers for the arm.
ArmControllerCLI creates a FollowJointTrajectory ActionClient on the absolute /joint_trajectory_controller/follow_joint_trajectory endpoint.
control_arm_cli.py imports control_msgs.action.FollowJointTrajectory.
ArmControllerCLI lists the seven controlled joints as joint1 through joint7 in that order.
ArmControllerCLI builds one JointTrajectoryPoint with positions and a time_from_start Duration, appends it to trajectory.points and sends the goal asynchronously.
The MoveIt simple controller manager names joint_trajectory_controller, type FollowJointTrajectory, action_ns follow_joint_trajectory and default true.
ros2_controllers.yaml configures joint_trajectory_controller for joint1 through joint7, with a position command interface and position and velocity state interfaces.
ros2_control.urdf.xacro declares gz_ros2_control/GazeboSimSystem and a position command interface with position, velocity and effort state interfaces for each of the seven joints.
gazebo_sim_ros2_control.urdf.xacro loads the gz_ros2_control::GazeboSimROS2ControlPlugin with the controller YAML path.
The Gazebo bringup bridges /joint_states as sensor_msgs/msg/JointState.
The Gazebo bringup bridge also carries /clock and /tf and starts a separate image bridge for the camera topics.
The arm xacro gives joint1, joint3, joint5 and joint7 the revolute range -6.28..6.28 rad and joint2, joint4 and joint6 the range -2.0..2.0 rad.
joint_limits.yaml sets max_velocity 2.0 for joint1 through joint4, 3.0 for joint5 and joint6, and 4.0 for joint7; max_acceleration is 1.0, 1.5 and 2.0 respectively.
initial_positions.yaml starts all seven joints at 0.0.
bcr_arm.gazebo.launch.py starts the Gazebo server and spawns the joint_state_broadcaster and joint_trajectory_controller controllers.
The launch's spawners name the controller manager /controller_manager.
The Gazebo launch's ros2_controllers_path defaults to bcr_arm_moveit_config's config/ros2_controllers.yaml.
The launch starts gz_sim with the -r argument, so the simulation runs from the start.
The controller manager creates the list_controllers service with the controller_manager_msgs::srv::ListControllers type under its private name.
The controller manager creates the switch_controller service with the controller_manager_msgs::srv::SwitchController type under its private name.
switch_controller_service_cb passes the request's controllers to activate and deactivate, its strictness, activate_asap and timeout to switch_controller and answers ok only when that returns OK.
switch_controller asks the realtime update loop for the switch and waits for it up to the request's timeout (1 s when it is zero); when the wait times out it clears the request and returns ERROR.
The controller manager's update loop performs a requested switch.
list_controllers fills each ControllerState with the controller's name, type, claimed interfaces and lifecycle state label.
SwitchController defines strictness STRICT as 2, under which the switch fails if anything goes wrong, and returns ok when the controllers were switched.
ControllerState's state field is unconfigured, inactive, active or finalized.
On deactivation the trajectory controller aborts an active goal, keeps each position command at its last value, releases its interfaces and drops its stored trajectory.

On activation the trajectory controller takes its current and last commanded state from the command interfaces when set_last_command_interface_value_as_state_on_activation is set and the command read succeeds, and otherwise reads both from the state interfaces.
set_last_command_interface_value_as_state_on_activation defaults to true: the last command interface value is then used as both the current state and the last commanded state on activation.
Reading the state from the command interfaces fails when the controller has a velocity state interface but no velocity command interface with values.
On activation the trajectory controller starts by holding the position of the state it starts from.
set_hold_position commands the positions of the controller's current state (state_current_).
The trajectory controller rejects a new action goal while it is inactive.
gz_ros2_control names its controller manager node controller_manager unless the SDF names another.
gz_ros2_control creates the controller manager in the plugin node's namespace and adds it to its executor.
gz_ros2_control writes the joint commands on every simulation step and reads and updates the controllers at the controller period.
For a position-controlled joint the Gazebo system turns the error to the position command into a target velocity.

determinism.notes: Event-driven recording stand-in with no physics step, trajectory interpolation, controller timing or wall-clock pacing; the placeholder joint samples do not establish trajectory or state-hash replay

gaps: the fake is a ROS-free recording transport: it answers the declared FollowJointTrajectory action and /joint_states subscriptions and runs no Gazebo, gz_ros2_control, MoveIt or ROS graph
the action goal is applied instantly to a placeholder seven-joint vector; there is no interpolation, timing, feedback, dynamics, gravity, collision or controller error behavior
the joint samples are placeholders; a live run must receive /joint_states from the operator's Gazebo bridge and the trajectory result from the operator's joint_trajectory_controller
the upstream image bridge, camera topics, /clock, /tf and the MoveIt planning interface are out of scope

the stop is the companion controller switch: the fake keeps the trajectory controller's lifecycle state, which switch_controller sets and list_controllers reports in a two-element controller list, and refuses goals while it is inactive; it runs no controller manager, update loop or lifecycle transition

deactivation keeps each joint's position command at its last value (joint_trajectory_controller.cpp:1069-1092), so a joint still converges to the last commanded point of the dropped trajectory; the world, the joint_state_broadcaster and /joint_states keep running

the switch waits up to 0.4 s for the controller manager's update loop (controller_manager.cpp:1307-1331), which gz_ros2_control drives from the simulation step: with the world paused the switch times out, answers ok false and the e-stop stays unconfirmed with the latch held (fails closed)
the read-back's list predicate selects the one element named joint_trajectory_controller (E4): none, two, or a state other than inactive leaves the e-stop unconfirmed

MoveIt, a controller spawner or any other ROS 2 client of /controller_manager/switch_controller can re-activate the controller after the e-stop; MHS does not watch its state afterwards (safety_status re-reads it only on request)

the deployment's controller_manager, joint_trajectory_controller and gz_ros2_control must be the pinned 2.54.4, 2.54.1 and 0.7.21 releases (Humble with Gazebo Fortress); the clone also documents Jazzy with Harmonic, which this package does not serve; rosbridge cannot read their versions

safe_state.description: joint_trajectory_controller is inactive, as list_controllers read back: its goal was aborted and its trajectory dropped, and each joint's position command keeps its last value, which the Gazebo system holds; the world keeps running, it is the controller's state, not a measured standstill, and any client can re-activate it.
